title: RBAC v2 Migration Risk Register (Hosted + Dedicated + Private)
content:
Purpose / how to use
- This register tracks known and anticipated migration risks as we move from RBAC v1 (coarse roles + inconsistent checks) to RBAC v2 (deny-by-default + permission inventory + auditable decisions).
- Primary audience: Security Eng, Platform Eng, PM, Release, Support/CS for enterprise pilots.
- Update cadence: 2x/week during pilot + rollout. Please add new risks as soon as discovered (even if mitigation TBD).

Scoring rubric (quick)
- Likelihood (L): 1=rare, 2=unlikely, 3=possible, 4=likely, 5=almost certain
- Impact (I): 1=minor annoyance, 2=localized support issue, 3=customer-visible degradation, 4=production incident / enterprise blocker, 5=security issue / compliance failure
- Priority: P = L x I (we treat >=12 as “needs active mitigation + monitoring plan”)

Current rollout assumptions (as of 2025-03-21)
- Dual-read mode (v1 + v2) supported behind feature flags for Hosted and Dedicated; Private uses bootstrap role binding on install.
- Deny-by-default in gateway; services must also enforce for sensitive endpoints (gateway is not a sole control).
- Authorization decision logging required for allow/deny and exported to SIEM for enterprise accounts.

Risk register (table)
Columns: Risk ID | Area | Risk statement | Trigger / example | L | I | P | Detection signals | Mitigation / controls | Owner | Status | Notes / links

R-01 | Gateway enforcement | Deny-by-default causes unexpected 403 spikes due to missing endpoint annotations or incorrect permission mapping | New endpoint ships without permission annotation; gateway middleware blocks | 4 | 4 | 16 | Increased 403 rate, “permission_denied” metrics, support tickets, synthetic checks failing | CI gate: fail build if sensitive routes unannotated; service-level tests; staged rollout by org; add dashboard for deny rate by route/model | Amara Diallo | Active | Linear ENG-18277 / ENG-18305; GitHub PR-28159

R-02 | Control plane services | Some control plane endpoints bypass authz due to legacy internal-only assumptions (or are called by Console with elevated service token) | Internal admin endpoint callable via customer path; missing interceptor | 3 | 5 | 15 | Security review findings; pen test; audit logs show “no_policy_evaluated=true” (should be zero) | Enforce shared interceptor lib; require authz context on all handlers; periodic endpoint audit diff; block merge on coverage regression | Ethan Park | Active | Links: endpoint audit doc; Linear ENG-18305

R-03 | Streaming routes | Authorization check bypass on streaming generation route (regression) | Route uses a different router/middleware chain; missed check | 2 | 5 | 10 | Incident alerts; route-level authz coverage test; log anomaly: streaming requests missing authz decision fields | Add regression test suite for streaming endpoints; standardize middleware; require authz decision logging even for streamed responses | Kaitlyn Nguyen | Mitigated | Hotfix PR-28391; Slack incident 1740151207

R-04 | Policy evaluator caching | Stale authorization decisions due to caching bugs (role changes not reflected quickly) | User removed from role still allowed for up to TTL; org admins rebind roles frequently during rollout | 3 | 5 | 15 | Audit log shows allow after role revoke; cache hit rate unusually high; customer reports “still has access” | Conservative TTL; cache key includes policy version + binding revision; invalidate on role/binding write; add metrics + canary tests | Jordan Lee | Active | GitHub PR-28203; Slack 1739808400

R-05 | Migration mapping | Default mapping from RBAC v1 roles to v2 permissions is incomplete (missing routing policy, audit export, key rotation) leading to customer breakage | Dedicated admin can’t edit routing policy; auditor can’t export logs | 4 | 4 | 16 | Support tickets during pilot; deny reason codes spike (MISSING_PERMISSION) | Maintain “compat mapping” bundle; preflight analyzer to compare v1 effective access vs v2; update role templates; customer comms | Naomi Feldman | Active | Jira SUP-48288, SUP-48219; Support Slack 1740065522

R-06 | Console UX | Console role editor / permission viewer confusing; admins misconfigure roles and lock themselves out | Overly granular permissions; unclear scope selection (org/project/env) | 3 | 3 | 9 | Increased support volume; time-to-resolution; drop-off in Console workflows | Add guided templates; “why denied” UX; safe defaults + warnings for high-impact permissions; add preview of effective permissions | Tessa Morgan | Active | Linear DES-914 / DES-927

R-07 | Break-glass | Break-glass elevation misused or insufficiently monitored (compliance/evidence risk) | Engineer uses break-glass for convenience; no post-review | 2 | 5 | 10 | Break-glass events without ticket; missing approvals; delayed alerting | Require approval workflow; time-bound elevation; alert SecOps on use; mandatory post-incident review; weekly audit | Fiona McCarthy | Active | Break-glass Confluence + INT-19103

R-08 | Audit logging | Missing or inconsistent authz decision fields in audit logs (allow/deny without reasons/policy version) harms SOC2 evidence and SIEM ingestion | Some services emit legacy audit events; exporter drops fields | 3 | 5 | 15 | Audit schema validation failures; SIEM mapping gaps; customer questionnaire failures | Schema contract tests; backfill required fields in emitter; exporter validation; rollout gating for enterprise orgs | Kevin Osei | Active | GitHub PR-28292; audit exporter PR-77

R-09 | Denial reason leakage | Denial reasons expose sensitive policy info to end users (information disclosure) | Debug header enabled broadly; errors reveal org structure or permission names | 3 | 4 | 12 | Security review; bug bounty reports; logs show debug headers in non-admin traffic | Default: generic “permission denied”; allow detailed reasons only for org admins + explicit header; strip in Hosted public API by default | Marcus Lin | Active | GitHub PR-28241; Slack 1740237345

R-10 | Performance | Added authz checks increase p95 latency for inference requests (especially chat/streaming) beyond SLO | Per-request remote evaluation; cache miss storms | 3 | 4 | 12 | Latency dashboards; evaluator call volume; cache miss rate | Prefer local evaluation library; safe caching; batch policy fetch; set budgets; load tests in staging; circuit-breaker to fail closed with clear errors | Priya Natarajan | Active | Fireflies: 2025-03-19 deep dive notes (latency)

R-11 | Private installer bootstrap | Private deployments fail to bootstrap initial admin role binding (first-login lockout) due to IdP group mapping mismatch | Customer installs Private; IdP group claim differs from docs | 3 | 4 | 12 | Installer logs; support escalations; customer unable to access Console | Provide “local bootstrap admin” with one-time token; preflight IdP claim validation; recovery runbook; SE onboarding checklist | Vivek Kulkarni | Active | GitHub:redwood-private-installer/pr-412; Linear ENG-18410

R-12 | Internal admin workflows | Redwood IT/admin users lose access to internal support/admin tools during dogfood (slows incident response) | Internal admin roles not including Console permissions; env scoping wrong | 4 | 3 | 12 | Internal tickets; on-call blocked from remediation actions | Define internal role templates; separate internal “Support Admin” vs “Security Admin”; dogfood checklist and access review | David Kim | Mitigated | INT-19022

R-13 | Cross-deployment semantics | Permission scope semantics differ across Hosted/Dedicated/Private (org vs project vs env vs cluster), causing inconsistent behavior and customer confusion | Same action allowed in Hosted but denied in Private due to different scope resolution | 3 | 4 | 12 | Pilot feedback; inconsistent audit log resource.scope fields | Document canonical scope model; enforce consistent resolver; add integration tests per deployment mode; SE training | Diego Santos | Active | Slack 1739482205; PM-661

R-14 | Data retention/residency controls | Permissions for retention/residency configuration not clearly separated (separation of duties requirement) | Billing admin can change audit retention or export settings | 2 | 4 | 8 | Enterprise questionnaire review; audit of role templates | Create dedicated “Security Admin” permission set; require two-person approval for high-risk config changes (phase 2) | Olga Petrov | Planned | Track in role templates + enterprise guidance

R-15 | Policy bundle versioning | Services run mismatched policy bundle versions leading to inconsistent allow/deny across regions | Canary uses new bundle but control plane still old | 3 | 3 | 9 | Audit logs show differing policy_version; region-to-region deny mismatch | Explicit bundle version pinning + rollout tooling; enforce “min required version” by service; alert on divergence | Connor O'Brien | Active | rbac-policy-bundle PR-184; release thread 1740582801

R-16 | Shadow endpoints / jobs | Background jobs / internal automation lack a clear subject identity and therefore fail authz (or run with overly broad service identity) | Key rotation job starts failing; audit export job runs with admin-like token | 3 | 4 | 12 | Job failure rates; audit logs show subject.type=service with broad scopes | Define service identities with minimal permissions; require explicit permission grants for jobs; add runbook for job authz failures | Benji Okafor | Active | Related: SUP-48305 (key rotation 403s)

R-17 | Supportability | “Permission denied” errors are hard to triage without correlating request IDs, scope, and evaluation trace | Support can’t tell if missing permission vs scope mismatch vs policy bundle bug | 4 | 3 | 12 | Long MTTR on permission-denied tickets; repeated back-and-forth | Standardize denial reason codes; include authz decision ID in response; provide internal-only debug endpoint; link to “why denied” in Console | Chloe Martin | Active | GitHub PR-28241; Support playbook draft

R-18 | Deny-by-default rollout | Feature flag misconfiguration enables RBAC v2 denies broadly (wrong cohort / env) | Flag toggled in production without ramp; affects all Hosted orgs | 2 | 5 | 10 | Sudden deny spike across many orgs; on-call alerts | Require change management + approvals for flags; progressive rollout tooling; rollback runbook; “kill switch” to revert to v1 checks | Connor O'Brien | Active | Rollout runbook + ENG-18388

Open questions / follow-ups
- Do we need a hard requirement that inference (data plane) routes have both gateway + service enforcement before GA for regulated customers? (Current stance: yes for any route handling customer tokens/keys; confirm with Platform.)
- What is the maximum acceptable propagation delay for role revocation in enterprise contracts? (We’re assuming “minutes” is acceptable with caching, but some financial prospects ask for “near real-time”.)
- Should we block enabling RBAC v2 for an org if their role templates deviate too far from recommended defaults (e.g., missing audit export permission for auditor role)?

Change log (manual)
- 2025-02-07: Added R-03 streaming route bypass after incident thread; marked mitigated post-hotfix.
- 2025-02-24: Added R-11 Private bootstrap lockout risk based on Private POC scoping call.
- 2025-03-06: Elevated R-05 priority after SUP-48288 + SUP-48219.
- 2025-03-21: Expanded R-04 caching risk with explicit invalidation plan; added R-15 policy bundle version divergence.

Notes to self (Olga)
- For SOC2 evidence package, we should point auditors to: (1) this risk register + updates, (2) PR links showing enforcement + tests, (3) audit log samples with authz context, (4) break-glass procedure + one completed review record (INT-19103) with redactions.
